A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentMath. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably despite the expanded appendix and section rearrangements.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, SFT/RL comparisons, data-refinement and scaling experiments, and training-efficiency analyses in Section 3 and Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original IMO-AnswerBench and GPQA evaluations, controlled comparisons, and synthesis and reward ablations in Appendices A.10-A.16.

M1.justification: Both versions retain segmented code injection, quality refinement and self-correction, selectively masked SFT, GRPO-based agentic RL, correctness-conditioned tool rewards, and asynchronous partial-rollout training. v3 supplies additional settings and component experiments without establishing a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained AIME24, AIME25, and HMMT25 evaluations, v3 adds the 400-problem IMO-AnswerBench and GPQA Diamond. The latter uses training examples sampled from Science 220K and extends coverage to physics, chemistry, and biology (Appendices A.11 and A.13.3).

E2.justification: The original comparator sets in Tables 1 and 4 remain. New controlled comparisons add ReTool-32B-SFT-2k and AM-Thinking-8B-SFT (Tables 8/25 and 26). Additional benchmark comparisons introduce models including GPT-5 and Grok 4 in Table 13 and Llama3.1-Nemotron-Nano-8B-v1 in Table 14.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a ReTool comparison controlling the 2k problems, teacher responses, backbone, and 400 RL steps; RL-data scaling at a fixed 200 steps; and reward ablations at 100 steps. v3 also introduces Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B backbone controls. The original main evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds segmentation-length and teacher-choice experiments, reward-component and coefficient ablations, RL-data scaling, and manual analyses of code complexity and replacement usefulness (Appendices A.12-A.16). These test previously unexamined design choices and confounders; the earlier refinement, SFT-scaling, and partial-rollout analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports 32 independent inference runs per original benchmark problem. v3 retains that practice, specifies eight-run evaluation for IMO-AnswerBench and GPQA, and reports eight independent training runs for the controlled distillation comparison in A.15. It adds no confidence intervals, run-level dispersion, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The original main tables retain AgentMath-30B-A3B's 90.6%, 86.4%, and 73.8% scores. v3 adds substantial results, including AgentMath-8B's 37.9% on IMO-AnswerBench, 58.9% on GPQA after science SFT, and new controlled-comparison and ablation outcomes. Table 9 also adds the tool-usage rationality refinement result, 57.2%/48.9%, absent from v1's Table 3.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, masked SFT loss, GRPO objective, reward equations, load-balancing equations, and partial-rollout algorithm are retained. Appendix A.16 restates existing reward mathematics, while A.12 explains the standard Jaccard formula for existing deduplication. No substantive new theoretical result, assumption, or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims about mathematical performance and scalable agentic training remain. Named proprietary-model comparisons newly emphasized in v3's abstract and introduction were already made in v1's conclusion and main-results discussion; they do not establish a new core claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning benchmark leakage, teacher-distillation confounding, segmentation failures, code-complexity filtering, reward choices, and applicability beyond mathematics. Appendix A.11 also newly argues that temporal controls eliminate contamination, a stronger conclusion than those controls alone establish.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 3k-token synthesis segments, the 0.6 deduplication threshold, explicit code-filtering and reward parameters, and hardware/time costs, including 128 GPUs with 96GB each and 62 hours for synthesis. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Some descriptions conflict: the added appendix names Qwen3-30B as verifier while retained Section 2.2 names Qwen3-32B.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 expands citations to RL infrastructure and related research, including OpenRLHF, RollPacker, and slime. Appendices A.10 and A.15 substantially expand positioning against ReTool/ToRL and teacher-distilled competitors, emphasizing synthesis scalability, long-sequence training, and controlled attribution of gains.

P1.justification: Although much existing prose remains unchanged, v3 brings data construction and training descriptions into new main-text Sections 3.1-3.3, adds a reproducibility statement, and introduces extensive explanatory appendices A.10-A.16. Repeated explanations of contributions, synthesis, and reward design substantially expand the narrative beyond the new experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 8-27, covering new evaluations and analyses alongside redisplayed results. For example, Table 11 repeats the existing efficiency table, and Table 12 summarizes retained benchmark results. Figures 1-9 remain, with Figures 6-7 relocated within the appendix; the main experimental layout also changes.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation through a larger mathematics benchmark, science evaluation, matched ReTool and distillation controls, and segmentation/reward ablations. Newly disclosed parameters and computational costs address important reproducibility gaps in v1. These gains outweigh substantial repetition and reporting weaknesses, including overly absolute contamination claims and the A.13.1 discrepancy between 7.8 tool calls in prose and 8.3 in Table 20.
